question: The hairy cell leukemia (hairy cell leukemia) presents as characteristic clinical-biological features:

options.opa: Lymphocytosis in peripheral blood greater than 50,000 lymphocytes / microL.
options.opc: Exfoliative generalized erythroderma, plaques and skin tumors.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Hairy cell leukemia" -> "B-cell neoplasm" -> "not T lymphoid line markers" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Hairy cell leukemia" -> "bone marrow infiltration" -> "pancytopenia" -> "decreased lymphocytes" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Hairy cell leukemia" -> "B-cell neoplasm" -> "not associated with skin manifestations" -> 75%
analysis: Hairy cell leukemia is a rare type of chronic leukemia characterized by the presence of abnormal B lymphocytes with 'hairy' projections. The disease typically presents with pancytopenia (a reduction in red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets) and splenomegaly (enlargement of the spleen). Lymphocytosis with extremely high lymphocyte counts, T lymphoid markers, or skin manifestations like erythroderma are not characteristic of hairy cell leukemia.
